_comment: ZeroBreach detection signatures, externalized from ZeroBreach-V23.ps1 so the engine's script body contains no malware-signature literals (avoids AMSI/Defender false positives). Loaded at runtime via Get-Content|ConvertFrom-Json — data files are not AMSI-scanned. Edit signatures here without touching the engine.
_comment_email_content_rules: Content-based signatures for HTML/JS phishing trojans (HTML smuggling, JS redirectors, obfuscated droppers). Applied to the CONTENT of small html/htm/js/hta/vbs/svg/log files found in email-attachment caches (Phase 74.5) and user paths (Phase 90). These match real malicious constructs, NOT antivirus signature NAMES, so they survive renaming and have low false-positive rates.
_comment_email_scan: Paths and extensions for Phase 74.5 (email-attachment malware scan). Paths use env-var tokens expanded at runtime. Deliberately EXCLUDES the bulk Outlook OST/PST data store (multi-GB, scanned separately) and targets only attachment-extraction / diagnostic caches where extracted trojans land.
_comment_proactive_hardening: Adversary-informed PROACTIVE safeguards. Each entry is a foothold a real attacker plants/abuses for execution, persistence or privilege escalation. Phase 74.7 audits these even when no active infection is found, so a freshly-cleaned box is hardened against re-infection rather than only scanned reactively.

_comment_fp_allowlists: False-positive allowlists (NOT malware signatures). Used to suppress/downgrade benign-but-noisy matches. Regex fragments are matched case-insensitively against file paths/names or cert subjects. Tune here without touching the engine.
_comment_beacon_benign_domains: Phase 59 DNS-beacon allowlist. Anchored to the registrable domain SUFFIX (optional trailing dot for a DNS-cache entry) because the beaconed name is entirely attacker-chosen: the previous bare-substring list ('microsoft|windows|google|...') was cleared by simply registering microsoft-update-cdn.example.com. NOTE: *.amazonaws.com is kept here for parity with the pre-2026-07-22 list even though it is commonly abused for C2 — high-frequency DNS is only a beacon HINT and the finding is Info-only, but revisit if FP pressure allows removing it.
_comment_trusted_root_ca_issuers: Phase 39 root-CA name hints. These are BARE WORDS matched against a certificate Subject/Issuer, which an attacker planting a MITM root fully controls ('CN=Microsoft Update CA' self-clears). They are therefore NO LONGER the primary trust signal — Phase 39 now decides on membership of the Microsoft-managed AuthRoot store (which the attacker cannot join) and on the store registry key's install time. This list only refines the wording of the finding.
_comment_cloaked_benign_names: Phase 18 (Hidden+System file scan). Matched against a FILENAME the attacker chooses, so every entry must pin the whole name (^...$) — the pre-2026-07-22 bare substrings 'iconcache'/'thumbcache'/'gdipfontcachev1.dat' let a cloaked payload evade the phase entirely by calling itself e.g. 'iconcache_svchost.exe'.
_comment_runkey_benign_values: Phase 20: matched against 'name = value' of Run/RunOnce entries. OneDrive writes its own cleanup RunOnce values (cmd.exe+del of its cached updater) — benign, downgraded to POSSIBLE/Info (never auto-DeleteReg). Patterns MUST pin the ENTIRE value to the exact benign command shape ($-anchored, no room for chained commands) or malware can name its value to self-allowlist. Covers both the machine-wide (\Microsoft OneDrive\) and per-user (\Microsoft\OneDrive\) install paths.
_comment_miner_config_benign_paths: Phase 63: config.json content heuristics (pools/stratum/mining words) hit legitimate app configs — LGHUB game-integration applets et al. Allowlisted parent paths downgrade to POSSIBLE/Info.
_comment_spooler_benign_dlls: Phase 96: Microsoft printer RESOURCE DLLs in spool\drivers are catalog-signed (invisible to Get-AuthSig, which only sees embedded Authenticode) and grade as UNSIGNED on every box with a PCL/PS driver. Known resource-DLL names downgrade to POSSIBLE/Info.
_comment_keylogger_benign_paths: Phase 48: keystroke-log *name* heuristics (*typed*, *capture*log*, …) inside package-manager trees are library files (e.g. py.typed markers), not keylogger output. Downgraded to POSSIBLE/Info.
_comment_yara_benign_paths: Phase 90: JIT/renderer runtime DLLs legitimately contain VirtualAllocEx/WriteProcessMemory-class API strings (SwiftShader et al. compile shaders at runtime); package-manager trees ship API-name-bearing sources. Rule hits here downgrade to POSSIBLE/Info instead of HIGH/DeleteFile.
_comment_sct_benign_paths: Phase 94: .sct/.wsc scriptlets inside package-manager trees are library test fixtures (e.g. pywin32's Testpys.sct), not Squiblydoo staging. Downgraded to POSSIBLE/Info.
_comment_c2_named_pipe_regex: Named-pipe backdoor patterns (Phase 62). Specific C2/RAT framework pipe names + known-malware terms ONLY. Must NOT include a broad hex/GUID match — most legit Windows RPC/COM/Ep-mapper pipes are GUID- or hex-named, so a catch-all floods CRITICAL false positives.
_comment_hidden_task_benign_paths: Scheduled-task FullNames (Phase 104) that legitimately ship <Hidden>true</Hidden> maintenance tasks. Matched case-insensitively against the task XML's full path. Known = INFO; unrecognized hidden tasks are NOT suppressed — they downgrade to POSSIBLE (surfaced for review, never auto-deleted). A hidden task is weak signal on its own.
_comment_bits_suspicious_remote: BITS job (Phase 31) escalation indicators. A BITS job is corroborating evidence, not a standalone HIGH (every Windows/app updater uses BITS). Default POSSIBLE; escalate to HIGH only when the job's remote URL is a raw IP, or it stages an executable/script into a user-writable path. NOT malware signatures — generic heuristics.
_comment_ws1_externalized: WS1 (2026-06-30): inline name-lists that read like AV signatures, moved out of engine/*.ps1 so the script body carries no signature literals (AMSI/portability hardening). Each key maps 1:1 to one phase. Content is the exact pre-externalization list — refreshing/expanding these families is WS2.
_comment_ws5_externalized: WS5 (2026-07-22 review #22): the last three inline name-lists left in .ps1 source after WS1. Commercial-keylogger vendor names, keystroke-log filename globs and browser-adware/hijacker extension names all read like AV signatures, so they belong in data (AMSI-safe) like every sibling list. Content is the exact pre-externalization list — no behaviour change.
_comment_ws2_expansion: WS2 (2026-06-30): detection-coverage expansion researched from public sources (MITRE, abuse.ch, CISA #StopRansomware, LOLDrivers, LOLBAS, SigmaHQ, vendor reports). All DATA / AMSI-safe. Point-in-time C2 domains/hashes are confirmation IOCs (many sinkholed) — the durable signals are the behavior rules, drop-path rules, ransom-note filenames, BYOVD driver names, and anchored C2 pipe regexes. Severities deliberately conservative.

_comment_ws6_expansion: WS6 (2026-07-22): detection expansion across credential/identity theft, modern intrusion TTPs, and persistence/evasion depth. Sourced from MITRE ATT&CK, CISA advisories, LOLBAS/LOLDrivers and public vendor reporting. Consumed by the new FRACTIONAL phases 17.5/20.5/32.5/44.5/45.5/51.5/68.5/82.5/100.5. Grading rule for this whole block (user decision 2026-07-22): hardening and lockdown actions are OPERATOR-ONLY — Info/POSSIBLE + RunCmd so they are never picked up by the CRITICAL/HIGH auto-select. Only unambiguous malware artifacts carry an auto-actionable severity, and then Quarantine (reversible) in preference to DeleteFile.
_comment_ifeo: Image File Execution Options / SilentProcessExit are legitimate debugging features that malware uses for both persistence and to neuter security tooling. A Debugger value on ANY executable is abnormal outside active development; the security-tool names below make it an escalation.
_comment_injection_dll_points: Phase 22.5. EMPTIED 2026-07-22 after review: the AppInit_DLLs entries duplicated Phase 22 one-for-one (same target, same CRITICAL + DeleteReg), and AppCertDlls is a SUBKEY whose values name the DLLs — reading it as a value on Session Manager always returned null, so that check never fired. Phase 22.5 now walks the AppCertDlls subkey directly and covers netsh helper DLLs and Winsock LSPs. Kept as a key so a future genuinely-value-shaped injection point can be added here without touching the engine.
_comment_cred_access: Credential-theft staging. The dump-FILE patterns are what a technician actually finds after the fact (the tool itself is usually long gone), so they matter more than the tool names. Matched case-insensitively against a filename.

cred_theft_cmdline_rules.Name: Comsvcs-MiniDump-LSASS
cred_theft_cmdline_rules.Why: rundll32 comsvcs.dll MiniDump is the signature-free way to dump LSASS

cred_theft_cmdline_rules.Name: Vssadmin-ShadowCopy-For-Hive-Theft
cred_theft_cmdline_rules.Why: a shadow copy is the standard way to read locked SAM/SYSTEM/NTDS files

cred_theft_cmdline_rules.Name: Cmdkey-Credential-Enumeration
cred_theft_cmdline_rules.Why: enumerates stored credentials — common early recon, also used by admins

_comment_accessibility_backdoor: Sticky-keys-class backdoors: replacing or IFEO-debugging an accessibility binary yields a SYSTEM shell from the pre-logon screen. The binaries are Microsoft-signed, so a HASH/signature check is the detection, not the name.

rdp_hardening_checks.Why: Remote Desktop is enabled — if it is not needed, disabling it removes a heavily brute-forced entry point

rdp_hardening_checks.Name: UserAuthentication

rdp_hardening_checks.Name: fSingleSessionPerUser

rdp_hardening_checks.Name: DisablePasswordSaving

_comment_shadow_admin: Hidden and shadow-admin accounts. SpecialAccounts\UserList with a 0 value hides an account from the logon screen and from Settings — a real Windows feature with almost no legitimate use on an endpoint, and a favourite of hands-on-keyboard intruders.
_comment_clickfix: ClickFix / fake-CAPTCHA / 'paste this to verify you are human' social engineering: the victim is told to press Win+R and paste an attacker-supplied command. The forensic residue is the RunMRU registry key — the command the user actually pasted into the Run dialog. Extremely high fidelity: no legitimate workflow puts an encoded PowerShell downloader in RunMRU.

clipboard_lure_rules.Why: base64-encoded PowerShell pasted into the Run dialog

clipboard_lure_rules.Name: ClickFix-RemoteDownloadCradle

clipboard_lure_rules.Name: ClickFix-ClipboardVerifyLure

clipboard_lure_rules.Name: ClickFix-ConhostHiddenLaunch
clipboard_lure_rules.Why: conhost --headless is used to hide a console window from the victim

_comment_rmm_abuse: Remote monitoring/management tooling abused for hands-on-keyboard access. USER RULE #2 APPLIES: Datto / CentraStage / Kaseya are this shop's own legitimate partner tooling and are deliberately ABSENT from this list. Everything here is still dual-use — an MSP may legitimately run any of it — so a plain install is INFO, and only a suspicious install PATH or a portable/unattended drop escalates it. Never auto-actionable.
_comment_token_theft: Cloud and session token theft. Access tokens survive MFA, so these files are now a primary objective for infostealers. Presence of the FILE is normal for a developer box — the detection is a token store being READ or STAGED by an unsigned user-path process, plus tokens copied into a staging directory (archive/clipboard/temp) which is never legitimate.
_comment_timestomp: Time-stomping: an attacker back-dates a dropped file so it blends into the system image and slips past time-scoped scans. Detected structurally (creation time newer than write time by a wide margin, or a zeroed/epoch timestamp), so there is nothing to signature. Bounded to executable content in user-writable paths to keep it quiet.
_comment_ws6_hardening: Operator-only hardening actions surfaced by the WS6 phases. All Info/POSSIBLE + RunCmd so the CRITICAL/HIGH auto-select can never fire them (user rule #1); the GUI's APPLY HARDENING button selects them as a group. Each command is idempotent and individually reversible.

ws6_hardening_actions.Name: RunAsPPL
ws6_hardening_actions.Why: LSA Protected Process Light stops most userland LSASS credential dumping

ws6_hardening_actions.Name: UseLogonCredential
ws6_hardening_actions.Why: WDigest caches cleartext passwords in LSASS memory when enabled

ws6_hardening_actions.Name: RestrictAnonymous
ws6_hardening_actions.Why: blocks anonymous enumeration of accounts and shares

ws6_hardening_actions.Name: SMB1
ws6_hardening_actions.Why: SMBv1 is unpatchable-by-design and the WannaCry/NotPetya propagation path

ws6_hardening_actions.Name: NoDriveTypeAutoRun
ws6_hardening_actions.Why: disables AutoRun/AutoPlay on every drive type — the classic USB worm vector

ws6_hardening_actions.Name: EnableScriptBlockLogging
ws6_hardening_actions.Why: records de-obfuscated PowerShell — the single most useful IR artifact on Windows

ws6_hardening_actions.Name: EnableMulticast
ws6_hardening_actions.Why: LLMNR/NBT-NS poisoning is the standard internal credential-relay attack (Responder)
ws6_hardening_actions.Fix: New-Item -Path 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows NT\DNSClient' -Force | Out-Null; Set-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows NT\DNSClient' EnableMulticast 0 -Type DWord -Force

ws6_hardening_actions.Name: ConsentPromptBehaviorAdmin
ws6_hardening_actions.Why: prompt-on-secure-desktop defeats the fodhelper-class silent auto-elevation bypasses

_comment_sitepackages: site-packages allowlist shape (fixed 2026-07-22 round 2): the tightening to '\\lib\\site-packages\\' broke Windows `pip install --user`, which lands in %APPDATA%\\Python\\Python3xx\\site-packages with NO Lib component — that re-armed Phase 48's CRITICAL+DeleteFile on py.typed marker files. The 'lib\\' segment is therefore optional. Note Test-BenignPath still vetoes a match found in a staging dir, so the looser form does not reopen the self-allowlisting hole it was tightened for.
_comment_ws7_expansion: WS7 (2026-07-25): detection expansion — DLL side-loading search-order-hijack target audit (Phase 32.5), browser-extension update_url pointing outside vendor endpoints (Phase 8), clipboard clipper co-occurrence (Phase 49.5), cloud IMDS credential-theft allowlist (Phase 36.5), npm/pip postinstall supply-chain exfil trusted-host allowlist (Phase 10.6). All DATA / AMSI-safe. Every detection here is POSSIBLE/HIGH + FixAction Info — none is auto-destructive on a healthy box (rule #1).
_comment_sideload: Phase 32.5: DLL search-order-hijack TARGET filenames (well-known DLL names Windows will silently load from an app's own directory before System32) and the signed EXE names commonly abused as the sideload host. Escalation to HIGH requires BOTH lists to match AND the pair to sit directly in an AppData/Temp/ProgramData root — see the phase body for the full gate; a bare name-list hit alone stays POSSIBLE.
_comment_extension_update_url: Phase 8 (Get-ExtensionRisk): official browser-vendor extension-update endpoints. A manifest update_url is attacker-controllable text (a side-loaded/malicious extension sets its own manifest), so every fragment is anchored to scheme+host so an attacker cannot self-allowlist by embedding one of these hostnames later in the URL path.
_comment_clipper: Phase 49.5: clipboard-API reference patterns and hardcoded cryptocurrency address patterns (BTC legacy/bech32, ETH 0x). NEITHER list alone is a finding — Test-ClipperCoOccurrence in the phase body requires BOTH to match the SAME piece of content (a Run/RunOnce value, scheduled-task command line, or recently-dropped script).
_comment_imds: Phase 36.5: legitimate cloud guest-agent process names / install paths permitted to reach the Instance Metadata Service (169.254.169.254). HIGH-FP-RISK by design (RMM/backup/monitoring agents poll this constantly on a healthy cloud VM) — hard-gated allowlist, POSSIBLE + Info regardless, never auto-actionable.
_comment_cloud_agent_names: Includes AWS/Azure/GCE/Docker guest agents PLUS common cloud-monitoring/observability agents that also legitimately poll the IMDS on a real production VM: CloudWatch unified agent (AWS), Azure Monitor Agent + legacy Microsoft Monitoring Agent (MonAgent*/MonitoringHost — AMA's Windows service is built on the same Geneva-derived binaries), Datadog Agent, New Relic Infrastructure Agent.
_comment_npm_postinstall: Phase 10.6: hosts npm postinstall/preinstall scripts legitimately fetch prebuilt binaries from at install time (electron-builder, playwright, puppeteer, node-gyp). Anchored to scheme+host (not a bare substring) — the postinstall script value this is matched against is attacker-controllable package.json content, so an unanchored fragment would let a malicious package self-allowlist by embedding the hostname elsewhere in its URL. This phase only ever parses package.json scripts.postinstall/preinstall (never setup.py/pyproject.toml), so the pypi.org/files.pythonhosted.org entries below are currently inert — kept for when pip-manifest parsing is added, not a live FP mitigation today. NOT enumerable here: private/enterprise npm registry mirrors (Artifactory/Nexus/Verdaccio) are fully site-specific — add your mirror's host as an additional anchored regex entry to suppress it (same customization path as every other allowlist in this file; no code change needed).
_comment_ws8_expansion: WS8 (2026-07-25) detection expansion — GPP cpassword decrypt (Phase 87.5), Kerberoasting/AS-REP roasting event triage (Phase 88.5), Outlook forward+hide BEC rule audit (Phase 74.8), SSH authorized_keys backdoor audit (Phase 77 extension), Office VSTO/COM add-in sideload (Phase 74 extension). The GPP regex + AES key below are exactly what every GPP-password-harvesting tool (PowerSploit Get-GPPPassword, CrackMapExec gpp_autologin) embeds inline — precisely the AMSI trip-wire rule #1 exists to keep out of the .ps1. All FixAction Info — none of these is auto-destructive on a healthy box.
_comment_ws9_expansion: WS9 (2026-07-26) detection expansion — PsExec/PAExec/RemCom lateral-movement literal service-name match (Phase 107 7045 extension), WSL Linux-side persistence/cron/dotfile staging (Phase 101 extension), MSIX/App Installer sideloading abuse (Phase 97.5, new), Chrome/Edge App-Bound-Encryption-bypass cookie-theft tooling (Phase 100.5 extension), Pass-the-Hash/NewCredentials logon triage (Phase 107 4624 extension), ComHandler scheduled-task trigger cross-correlated with COM hijack (Phase 104 extension + Phase 105 correlation). The PsExec-family literal-name match stays CRITICAL severity (near-zero legitimate software installs a service literally named PSEXESVC) but FixAction Info — nothing live to safely kill/delete from a historical event-log correlation. Everything else here is POSSIBLE + Info.
_comment_wsl_dev_benign: Phase 101: suppresses the WSL cron/dotfile persistence heuristic (raw-IP download / /mnt/c .exe cross-launch) for common legitimate WSL<->Windows developer-interop patterns. Matched per-LINE (never against the whole crontab/dotfile blob) and full-line-anchored with a bounded no-shell-metacharacter tail ([^&|;]*) so a malicious line on its own cannot be suppressed by an unrelated benign line elsewhere in the same file, and a single line can't smuggle a chained malicious command past the anchor. Seeded conservatively — this heuristic has moderate-to-high FP risk on real developer boxes and stays POSSIBLE-only, never escalated.
_comment_abe_bypass: Phase 100.5: known Chrome/Edge App-Bound-Encryption-bypass cookie-theft tool names (2024-2025 stealer generation that reads cookies/tokens via IPC to the browser's elevation service instead of touching the credential DB, so Phase 100's access-time check is blind to it). COVERAGE GAP, NOTED ON PURPOSE: publicly-documented tool names for this technique are sparse and often polymorphic/renamed per campaign, so this list is intentionally minimal rather than guessed — seeded with the one consistently-named public PoC (ChromeKatz). Matched only against unsigned processes/files sitting in a user-writable path (never a bare name match anywhere) to keep FP risk low; POSSIBLE + Info.
